plants.name: Aster novi-belgii
plants.description: A clump-forming perennial native to eastern North America, covered in daisy-like flower heads with yellow centers. It is a late-season nectar source for migrating monarch butterflies and many native bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern North America; widely cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The name Aster comes from the Greek word for star, and asters were once burned by ancient peoples to drive away serpents.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped flowers in autumn without any leaves present. The leaves emerge the following spring and die back by early summer. It is not a true crocus and all parts are highly toxic.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges of Europe, from Britain to the Balkans; grown in gardens in temperate regions
plants.funFact: It is nicknamed 'naked ladies' because the flowers appear without leaves, and it is the source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine and plant breeding.

plants.name: Lycoris radiata
plants.description: A striking bulbous plant with spidery, recurved red flowers and long protruding stamens on bare stalks. The narrow leaves appear after flowering and persist through winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Native to China, Korea and Japan; naturalized in the southeastern United States
plants.funFact: In Japan it blooms around the autumn equinox, called Higan, and is strongly associated with that Buddhist season, often planted along rice paddies and cemeteries.

plants.name: Watsonia borbonica
plants.description: A cormous perennial with tall spikes of tubular pink flowers rising above sword-shaped leaves. It thrives in sunny, well-drained sites and flowers as the Southern Hemisphere spring begins.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (September to November)
plants.location: Western Cape of South Africa fynbos; naturalized in parts of Australia and elsewhere
plants.funFact: Fynbos plants like this one often flower most profusely after fire, as the smoke and cleared ground trigger blooming.
